Step 1: Understand the context of the Confederate States Army. The Confederate States Army was the military land force of the Confederate States of America during the American Civil War, which lasted from 1861 to 1865.
Step 2: Recognize the outcome of the American Civil War. The Confederacy surrendered in 1865, and the Confederate States Army was dissolved and ceased to exist at that time.
Step 3: Consider the mortal lifespan of the individuals who served in the Confederate States Army. Anyone who was enlisted in the Confederate Army during the Civil War would have had to be born by the mid-19th century at the latest. Consequently, all Confederate veterans have passed away (the last verified Confederate veteran, Moore Winchester, died in the 1950s, or depending on disputed claims, John King or Pleasant Crump died in the 1950s as well).
Step 4: Conclude that because the army no longer exists and all its members have passed away, there are no Americans currently enlisted in the Confederate States Army.
